chunks: What Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from Muḥammad ibn Sahl, from his father, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a person performing ʿumrah who resides in Makkah: should he perform hajj ifrād, or should he perform tamattuʿ once again? He said: Performing tamattuʿ is more beloved to me, and let his ihram be from the distance of a journey of one night or two nights.

key_terms.إِحْرَامُهُ: his state of ihram for the rite
key_terms.الْمُقِيمِ: one residing or staying in a place
key_terms.مَسِيرَةِ لَيْلَةٍ: the distance of one night's travel
key_terms.يُجَرِّدُ الْحَجَّ: to perform hajj alone, i.e. separately without tamattuʿ

ai.seo_question: Should a resident of Makkah perform hajj ifrād or hajj al-tamattuʿ after ʿumrah?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling for a resident in Makkah who has performed ʿumrah and asks whether he should perform hajj ifrād or hajj al-tamattuʿ again. Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام states that tamattuʿ is preferable, and instructs that the ihram should be entered from the distance of one or two nights’ travel.
